summary: Iteration 4 full regression PASSED. Backend: 30/30 pytest (added 7 new date-night tests: auth-required, list, create w/ persistence, partner visibility, status update + GET verification, delete + GET verification, unpaired-user 400). Frontend: Logged in as Alice, dashboard loads with DATE NIGHT PLANNER section visible, Next Date Night card shows 'Movie Night: Stranger Things' with countdown 'in 6 days' + Sat, Apr 25 / 20:00 / 'Watching: Stranger Things' / 'Grab popcorn and blankets!', Upcoming 'Rom-Com Marathon' visible (Sat, May 2 at 19:30), Plan button opens dialog with title input + date picker + time selector + optional movie + notes, Calendar picker shows current month with 21 past days DISABLED (confirmed via DOM query), created 'TEST_UI_Night' successfully via the dialog (appeared on dashboard), Mark Complete fired toast 'Hope you had a great time!' and moved item to PAST with strikethrough, Delete removed item from list. Watchlist section still renders. Navigation to /watch works and chat input is visible.

issues: Complete/delete action buttons are hidden until hover (opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100) - not discoverable on touch devices; consider always-visible with lower opacity or a kebab menu on mobile.
'Offline' badge low contrast on pastel bg (carry-over from iter 1-3, non-blocking).

critical_code_review_comments: DateNightPlanner.js: PUT /api/date-nights/{id} endpoint accepts any field subset (title/date/time/movie/notes/status) but frontend only sends {status:'completed'} on markComplete - good; no edit flow is exposed to users yet (create-only). Consider adding an edit dialog in a future iteration.

DateNightPlanner.js line 127: past filter uses `isPast(new Date(\`${n.date}T23:59:59\`))` without timezone - may incorrectly flip a date to 'past' for users in late-offset timezones. Acceptable for MVP but worth noting.

server.py /api/date-nights PUT has no Pydantic model for the body (accepts raw request.json) and silently ignores unknown keys - low risk but deviates from the rest of the API which uses BaseModel. Consider a DateNightUpdateReq model with optional fields for consistency/validation.
server.py /api/date-nights DELETE returns 200 even when the night_id does not exist or belongs to another couple - idempotent-delete is acceptable but a 404 would be stricter.

Auth playbook spot-check: bcrypt hash stored starts with $2b$ (verified via login roundtrip), httpOnly cookies set on login (access_token + refresh_token), CORS allow_credentials is True when origins are explicit, seed_admin is idempotent (find_one->insert_one guarded). NOTE: no brute-force lockout is implemented (iter-1..4) - out of scope for this feature but flag for future.
